frames.narration: A viewer taps ad 42 at 12:00:58, but the phone is in a lift and has no signal. The click is saved on the phone with its event time and its click id, c-9f, which was issued when the ad was shown, so a retry will carry the same id.
At 12:01:20 the phone is online again and sends the click. The collector checks the signed token and passes the click to the fraud filter, which finds a normal rate for this device.
The click is appended to the log, in the partition for ad 42, and the collector answers the phone at once. From here on the counting can be slow without losing anything.

The aggregator reads the click. Its event time, 12:00:58, puts it in the 12:00 window, not the 12:01 window in which it arrived. It checks the click id store: c-9f has not been seen, so it is recorded.

The watermark is the newest event time seen, 12:01:30, minus the allowed lateness of 30 seconds, so it is 12:01:00. That is the end of the 12:00 window, so the window is final. Its total of 1,204 clicks is written to the store, replacing any earlier value.

A second phone had been offline longer. Its click, for 12:00:40, arrives at 12:01:45, after the window closed. It is not dropped. It goes to the late-events output, and a correction adds it to the stored total, which becomes 1,205.

The first phone retries, because it never saw the earlier reply. The retry carries the same id, c-9f. The aggregator asks the click id store, hears it has been counted already, and ignores it, so the total stays at 1,205.

Overnight, the batch job recounts the day from the raw archive, with all late clicks, exact dedup and the final fraud rules. It finds 7 bot clicks the live filter let through, so the correct figure is 1,198. It overwrites the stored total, and this is the number the advertiser is billed on.
